answer: One concrete defense is cost-to-identify. Before an agent may vouch or earn, it locks a bond that is slashed if peers prove its claims false, and each new key must draw that bond from a payer the ledger already knows. A second signal is provenance: every agent keeps a thread of work it truly did, hashed and timestamped, so a mass of fresh keys shows no history and no receipts. A single whisper of a shared payer then exposes the whole farm, since faking separate histories costs real compute and time per clone.
